title: Homily I — Death made blessed, and her burial

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily I on the Dormition, cols. 717-720 (PDF leaves 400-401)

source_text: Ὦ θαύματος ὄντως ὑπερφυοῦς! ὦ πραγμάτων ἐκπλήξεως. Ὁ πάλαι βδελυκτὸς καὶ μισούμενος θάνατος, καὶ εὐφημεῖται καὶ μακαρίζεται. Ὁ πάλαι πένθους καὶ κατηφείας, δακρύων τε καὶ σκυθρωπότητος πρόξενος, νῦν χαρᾶς ἀναδέδεικται καὶ πανηγύρεως αἴτιος. Ὅμως εἰ καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς τοῦ Θεοῦ θεράπουσιν, ὧν ὁ θάνατος μακαρίζεται, ἐκ τοῦ τέλους τὸ ἀσφαλὲς περιγίνεται τῆς πρὸς Θεὸν εὐαρεστήσεως, καὶ τούτου χάριν ὁ θάνατος αὐτῶν μακαρίζεται. Τελειοῖ γὰρ αὐτοὺς, καὶ μακαρίους δείκνυσι, τὸ ἄτρεπτον τῆς ἀρετῆς χαριζόμενος, κατὰ τὸ φάσκον λόγιον· μὴ μακάριζε ἄνδρα πρὸ τελευτῆς αὐτοῦ· ἀλλ' οὐκ ἐπὶ σοὶ τοῦτο ληψόμεθα. Σοῦ γὰρ μακαρισμὸς, οὐχ ὁ θάνατος· οὐδὲ ἡ μετάστασις τελείωσις γέγονεν, οὐδ' αὖ πάλιν ἡ ἐκδημία χαρίζεται τὴν ἀσφάλειαν. Πάντων γὰρ σὺ τῶν ὑπὲρ νοῦν ἀγαθῶν ἀρχὴ, καὶ μεσότης, καὶ τέλος, ἀσφάλειά τε καὶ ἀληθὴς βεβαίωσις, ἡ ἄσπορος σύλληψις, ἡ θεία ἐνοίκησις, ὁ τόκος ὁ ἄφθορος γέγονεν. Ὅθεν ἀληθῶς ἔφησας, οὐκ ἀπὸ τοῦ θανάτου, ἀλλ' ἐξ αὐτῆς τῆς συλλήψεως ὑπὸ πασῶν τῶν γενεῶν μακαρίζεσθαι. Ἐντεῦθεν οὐ σὲ ὁ θάνατος ἐμακάρισεν, ἀλλ' αὐτὴ τὸν θάνατον κατηγλάϊσας, τὴν τούτου κατήφειαν λύσασα, καὶ χαρὰν τὸν θάνατον δείξασα. Ὅθεν σου τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ πανάμωμον σῶμα ὁσίᾳ ταφῇ παρεδίδοτο, προτρεχόντων ἀγγέλων, περικυκλούντων, ἑπομένων, μήτι πραττόντων ὧν εἰκὸς τῇ μητρὶ τοῦ ἑαυτῶν λειτουργῆσαι Δεσπότου, ἀποστόλων, καὶ παντὸς τοῦ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας πληρώματος θεηγορικοὺς ὕμνους ἐκβοώντων, καὶ κροτουμένων τῷ πνεύματι· Πλησθησόμεθα ἐν τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς τοῦ οἴκου σου· ἅγιος, ὁ ναός σου, θαυμαστὸς ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ. Καὶ πάλιν· Ἡγίασε τὸ σκήνωμα αὐτοῦ ὁ Ὕψιστος. Ὄρος τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὄρος πῖον· τὸ ὄρος ὃ εὐδόκησεν ὁ Θεὸς κατοικεῖν ἐν αὐτῷ. Σὲ τῶν ἀποστόλων ὁ δῆμος τὴν ἀληθῆ κιβωτὸν Κυρίου τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπὶ τῶν ὤμων ἀράμενοι, ὡς πάλαι ποτὲ οἱ ἱερεῖς τὴν τυπικὴν κιβωτὸν, καὶ ἐν τάφῳ θέμενοι, δι' αὐτοῦ, ὡς δι' Ἰορδάνου τινὸς, ἐπὶ τὴν ἀληθῆ τῆς ἐπαγγελίας παρέπεμπον γῆν, τὴν ἄνω φημὶ Ἱερουσαλὴμ, τὴν πάντων τῶν πιστῶν μητέρα, ἧς τεχνίτης καὶ δημιουργὸς ὁ Θεός. Οὐ κατελήλυθε γὰρ ἡ ψυχή σου εἰς τὸν ᾅδην, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ ἡ σάρξ σου εἶδε διαφθοράν. Οὐκ ἀπελείφθη ἐν γῇ τὸ σὸν ἄχραντον καὶ πανακήρατον σῶμα, ἀλλ' ἐν οὐρανῶν βασιλείοις μοναῖς ἡ βασιλὶς, ἡ κυρία, ἡ δέσποινα, ἡ Θεομήτωρ, ἡ ἀληθὴς Θεοτόκος μετατεθεῖσα.
pass_a_gloss: O wonder (θαῦμα) truly beyond-nature (ὑπερφυής)! O astonishment (ἔκπληξις) of the events. Death (θάνατος), formerly abominable (βδελυκτός) and hated, is both well-spoken-of (εὐφημεῖται) and called blessed. The formerly procurer (πρόξενος) of mourning (πένθος) and dejection (κατήφεια), tears and gloom, now has been shown cause (αἴτιος) of joy and festival (πανήγυρις). Yet even if for all the servants (θεράπων) of God, whose death is called blessed, from the end (τέλος) there accrues the security (τὸ ἀσφαλές) of well-pleasing toward God, and for this reason their death is called blessed: for it perfects (τελειοῖ) them and shows them blessed, granting the unchangeableness (τὸ ἄτρεπτον) of virtue (ἀρετή), according to the saying (λόγιον): do not call a man blessed before his end (τελευτή); but we will not take (λαμβάνω) this in your case. For your blessedness (μακαρισμός) is not the death; nor did the removal (μετάστασις) become perfection (τελείωσις), nor again does the departure-abroad (ἐκδημία) grant the security. For [as for] you, of all the goods beyond mind (ὑπὲρ νοῦν) the beginning, middle (μεσότης), end, security and true confirmation (βεβαίωσις) has become (γέγονεν) the seedless conception, the divine indwelling (ἐνοίκησις), the incorrupt birth. Hence truly you said, not from death but from the conception itself, [you would] be called blessed by all generations. Thence death did not bless you, but you yourself made death resplendent (κατηγλάϊσας), loosing its dejection, showing death [to be] joy. Hence your holy and all-blameless (πανάμωμον) body was handed over to holy burial (ταφή), angels running before, encircling, following, [printed μήτι] doing the things fitting to minister to the mother of their own Master (Δεσπότης); apostles and the whole fullness (πλήρωμα) of the Church crying out God-spoken (θεηγορικούς) hymns and being struck/sounded (κροτουμένων) by the Spirit: We shall be filled with the goods of your house; holy your temple (ναός), wondrous in righteousness. And again: The Most High sanctified his tent (σκήνωμα). Mountain of God, fat mountain (ὄρος πῖον); the mountain which God was pleased (εὐδόκησεν) to dwell in. You, the true ark (κιβωτός) of the Lord God, the people (δῆμος) of the apostles, raising on their shoulders, as once the priests the typical (τυπική) ark, and placing in a tomb, through it as through a kind of Jordan escorted (παρέπεμπον) to the true land of the promise (ἐπαγγελία), I mean the Jerusalem above, the mother of all the faithful, whose craftsman (τεχνίτης) and maker (δημιουργός) [is] God. For your soul did not go down to Hades (ᾅδης), nor did your flesh (σάρξ) see corruption (διαφθορά). Your immaculate (ἄχραντον) and all-undefiled (πανακήρατον) body was not left on earth, but to the royal mansions of heavens [was] translated (μετατεθεῖσα) the queen (βασιλίς), the lady (κυρία), the mistress (δέσποινα), the God-mother (Θεομήτωρ), the true God-bearer (Θεοτόκος).
pass_b_english: O wonder truly beyond nature! O astonishing events! Death, once loathed and hated, is now praised and called blessed. What once brought mourning and gloom, tears and sadness, has now been shown to be the cause of joy and festival. It is true that for all the servants of God whose death is called blessed, it is the end that brings the security of having pleased God, and for this reason their death is called blessed. For death perfects them and shows them to be blessed, granting that their virtue can no longer change, according to the saying: 'Call no one blessed before his death' (Sirach 11:28). But we shall not take this to apply to you. For your blessedness is not your death; your passing did not become your perfecting, nor does your departure bestow your security. For in your case the beginning, the middle and the end of all the good things that pass understanding, and their security and true confirmation, were the conception without seed, the divine indwelling and the birth without corruption. That is why you truly said that you would be called blessed by all generations (Luke 1:48), not from your death but from the conception itself. So death did not make you blessed; rather, you made death glorious, undoing its gloom and showing death to be joy. And so your sacred and all-blameless body was given over to a holy burial. Angels ran before it, surrounded it and followed it, doing whatever it was fitting to do in service of the mother of their own Master, while the apostles and the whole fullness of the Church cried aloud hymns inspired by God, set ringing by the Spirit: 'We shall be filled with the good things of your house; holy is your temple, wonderful in righteousness' (Psalm 65:4–5). And again: 'The Most High has sanctified his dwelling' (Psalm 46:4). 'The mountain of God, a rich mountain, the mountain in which God was pleased to dwell' (Psalm 68:15–16). The company of the apostles lifted you, the true ark of the Lord God, on their shoulders, as once the priests lifted the ark that was a figure (Joshua 3:14–17); and laying you in a tomb, they escorted you through it, as through a kind of Jordan, to the true land of promise, I mean the Jerusalem above, the mother of all the faithful (Galatians 4:26), whose designer and maker is God (Hebrews 11:10). For your soul did not go down into Hades, nor did your flesh see corruption (Psalm 16:10). Your undefiled and all-pure body was not left behind on earth; you have been carried over to the royal dwellings of heaven, you the Queen, the Lady, the Sovereign, the Mother of God, she who truly gave birth to God.

choices.note: Sirach 11:28 is printed in the margin as 'Eccli. xi, 30' (older Vulgate numbering);
Greek wording 'μὴ μακάριζε ἄνδρα πρὸ τελευτῆς' matches Sirach 11:28.
Psalm renumbering (LXX/Vulgate to English): LXX 64:5-6a = Psalm 65:4-5 ('πλησθησόμεθα ...
θαυμαστὸς ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ' runs over the LXX verse break);
LXX 45:5 = Psalm 46:4;
LXX 15:10 = Psalm 16:10 (wording also close to Acts 2:27, 31;
'οὐκ ἀπελείφθη' echoes Acts 2:31 'οὔτε ἐγκατελείφθη').
Joshua 3:14-17 cited for the priests carrying the ark through the Jordan into the land of promise (clear typology; not in the margin).
Galatians 4:26 and Hebrews 11:10 are unmarked in the margin but clear (Hebrews 11:10 is near word for word: 'ἧς τεχνίτης καὶ δημιουργὸς ὁ θεός').
Doubtful reading: 'μήτι πραττόντων' printed thus; rendered by sense as 'doing whatever it was fitting to do' (μή τι / τί οὐ would give 'leaving nothing undone'; the gist is the same).
'κροτουμένων τῷ πνεύματι' (passive of κροτέω, 'struck, made to sound') rendered 'set ringing by the Spirit'; the image of instruments is implied, not stated.
Edition note (16): Germ. and Colb. read ὀργάνου for Ἰορδάνου; rejected as senseless, with the edition.
'βασιλείοις μοναῖς' may echo John 14:2 (μοναί); possible only, left uncited.
Θεομήτωρ rendered 'Mother of God', ἀληθὴς Θεοτόκος 'she who truly gave birth to God' to keep the two titles distinct.
Review: 'Πάντων γὰρ σὺ ...
ἀρχή, καὶ μεσότης, καὶ τέλος ...

ἡ ἄσπορος σύλληψις, ἡ θεία ἐνοίκησις, ὁ τόκος ὁ ἄφθορος γέγονεν' construed with σύ as a hanging nominative ('in your case'): the conception, indwelling and birth are the subject of γέγονεν and map onto beginning, middle and end, answering the argument that for others security comes from the end (death).

The facing Latin of PG 96 col. 718 confirms ('Omnium enim bonorum initium, mediumque et finis, securitas etiam et vera confirmatio, in illa seminis experte conceptione, in illa divina inhabitatione, in illo sine labe partu constitit').
The same Latin renders μήτι πραττόντων as 'nullum denique obsequii genus praetermittentibus' and κροτουμένων τῷ πνεύματι as 'ad Spiritus lyram pulsatos', supporting the renderings kept.

changes: Fixed wrong sense in 'Πάντων γὰρ σὺ ... γέγονεν': conception, indwelling and birth are the beginning, middle and end of her goods (not Mary herself); Pass A matched; confirmed by facing Latin col. 718
Fronted object 'You, the true ark ... the company of the apostles lifted' reordered to plain English; παρέπεμπον rendered 'escorted'
ἱερὸν σῶμα rendered 'sacred' to keep it distinct from ὁσίᾳ ταφῇ 'holy burial'
